Failure to Adapt: Accessibility Standards in Provincial Building Codes

ABSTRACT
Provincial building codes across Canada have been slow to incorporate universal design principles despite two decades of accessibility legislation.1 This comment surveys the gap between legislative intent and code-level implementation.2

DISCUSSION
The Accessible Canada Act sets ambitious national goals but does not itself amend the building codes that govern most construction decisions.3 Provinces retain near-total discretion over the technical standards that determine whether a building is genuinely accessible.

CONCLUSION
Meaningful accessibility reform will require coordinated amendments to provincial building codes, not federal aspirational language alone.

1. Accessible Canada Act, SC 2019, c 10.
2. See CSA Group, B651-18: Accessible Design for the Built Environment.
3. Ibid.
